supporting_quotes.exact: The order in which elements are added to or removed from a stack is described as last in, first out, referred to by the acronym LIFO.

observations.subject: the order in which elements are added to or removed from a stack

claims.rationale: 引文 evidence-d286628a0b15（原文 [0,131)）逐字表述 "The order in which elements are added to or removed from a stack is described as last in, first out, referred to by the acronym LIFO."，与 claim 完全对应：LIFO 即后进先出，术语与定义与引文一致，无增补内容。

supporting_quotes.exact: As with a stack of physical objects, this structure makes it easy to take an item off the top of the stack, but accessing a datum deeper in the stack may require removing multiple other items first.

observations.subject: this structure (stack)
observations.predicate: makes it easy to take an item off the top, but accessing a datum deeper
observations.object: may require removing multiple other items first

claims.rationale: 引文 evidence-d10e607c26e6（原文 [0,198)）以实物堆叠作类比："easy to take an item off the top of the stack, but accessing a datum deeper in the stack may require removing multiple other items first"，与 claim 各分句逐字对应（从栈顶取元素容易、访问更深元素需先移除多个元素）。

supporting_quotes.exact: Additionally, a peek operation can, without modifying the stack, return the value of the last element added (the item at the top of the stack).

observations.subject: a peek operation
observations.predicate: can, without modifying the stack, return
observations.object: the value of the last element added (the item at the top of the stack)

claims.rationale: 引文 evidence-4593be24621b（原文 [0,143)）逐字支持："a peek operation can, without modifying the stack, return the value of the last element added (the item at the top of the stack)"，三个要点（peek、不修改栈、返回最后加入元素即栈顶项）全部有引文依据。

supporting_quotes.exact: Considered a sequential collection, a stack has one end which is the only position at which the push and pop operations may occur, the top of the stack, and is fixed at the other end, the bottom.

observations.subject: a stack (considered a sequential collection)
observations.predicate: has one end as the only position for push/pop (the top), and is fixed

claims.rationale: 引文 evidence-13a035e39fcd（原文 [0,195)）表述："a stack has one end which is the only position at which the push and pop operations may occur, the top of the stack, and is fixed at the other end, the bottom"，与 claim 完全一致（顺序集合、唯一操作端为栈顶、另一端底部固定）。

supporting_quotes.exact: A stack may be implemented to have a bounded capacity. If the stack is full and does not contain enough space to accept another element, the stack is in a state of stack overflow.

observations.subject: a stack with bounded capacity
observations.predicate: is in a state of stack overflow if
observations.object: full, without enough space to accept another element

claims.rationale: 引文 evidence-4dc02e593e5a（原文 [0,179)）逐字支持："A stack may be implemented to have a bounded capacity. If the stack is full and does not contain enough space to accept another element, the stack is in a state of stack overflow."，有界容量与栈溢出条件的表述与 claim 一致。

supporting_quotes.exact: A stack can be easily implemented either through an array or a linked list, as it is merely a special case of a list. In either case, what identifies the data structure as a stack is not the implementation but the interface: the user is only allowed to pop or push items onto the array or linked list, with few other helper operations.
A stack may be implemented as, for example, a singly linked list with a pointer to the top element.

observations.subject: a stack
observations.predicate: can be implemented via array or linked list; identified by interface not implementation; only pop/push allowed
observations.object: user operations on the underlying array or linked list

observations.subject: a stack
observations.object: a singly linked list with a pointer to the top element

claims.rationale: 两条引文共同支持 claim：evidence-322b64c2a9f2（原文 [0,335)）说明可用数组或链表实现、栈只是 list 特例、标识为栈的是接口而非实现、用户仅可 pop/push；evidence-78c22ee5ee5f（原文 [0,99)）给出具体示例——指向栈顶元素的单链表实现。两引文同源互补、无冲突，claim 各分句均有对应引文。

supporting_quotes.exact: The push operation adds an element and increments the top index, after checking for overflow:
Similarly, pop decrements the top index after checking for underflow, and returns the item that was previously the top one:

observations.subject: the push operation
observations.predicate: adds an element and increments the top index, after checking for overflow

observations.subject: pop
observations.predicate: decrements the top index after checking for underflow, and returns
observations.object: the item that was previously the top one

claims.rationale: 两条引文分别逐字描述 push 与 pop：evidence-1fae9bf0b3f4（原文 [0,93)）"adds an element and increments the top index, after checking for overflow"；evidence-57bb10891387（原文 [0,123)）"decrements the top index after checking for underflow, and returns the item that was previously the top one"。二者同属一个上下文的对称描述，互不冲突，claim 全部要素（检查溢出/下溢、递增/递减 top、返回原栈顶元素）均有依据。

supporting_quotes.exact: Calculators that employ reverse Polish notation use a stack structure to hold values. Expressions can be represented in prefix, postfix or infix notations and conversion from one form to another may be accomplished using a stack. Many compilers use a stack to parse syntax before translation into low-level code.

observations.subject: stack
observations.object: RPN calculator values; prefix/postfix/infix conversion; compiler syntax parsing before low-level code generation

claims.rationale: 引文 evidence-63eafcee671c（原文 [0,311)）逐句覆盖 claim 三个分句：逆波兰表示法计算器用栈保存值（"use a stack structure to hold values"）、前缀/后缀/中缀表示及相互转换可用栈完成（"conversion from one form to another may be accomplished using a stack"）、编译器用栈解析语法后再翻译为低级代码（"parse syntax before translation into low-level code"）。无任何超出引文的内容。

supporting_quotes.exact: Another important application of stacks is backtracking.
This can be achieved through the use of stacks, as a last correct point can be pushed onto the stack, and popped from the stack in case of an incorrect path.

observations.subject: backtracking
observations.predicate: is achieved by pushing a last correct point onto the stack and popping it in case of an incorrect path

claims.rationale: 回溯主题与机制完全有据：evidence-4fe264776635（原文 [0,56)）指出栈的重要应用是回溯；evidence-a7ae1699eb8d（原文 [0,157)）说明机制——最后正确点入栈、遇到不正确路径则弹出。但 claim 末尾括号示例"（如迷宫寻路）"未见于任何引文：引文只提及"an incorrect path"场景，未提及迷宫（maze）或寻路，该示例部分缺乏引文支撑，故为部分支持。

supporting_quotes.exact: There is also a number of small microprocessors that implement a stack directly in hardware, and some microcontrollers have a fixed-depth stack that is not directly accessible.

observations.subject: a number of small microprocessors / some microcontrollers
observations.predicate: implement a stack directly in hardware / have a fixed-depth stack

claims.rationale: 引文 evidence-def936ce83dc（原文 [0,176)）逐字支持："a number of small microprocessors that implement a stack directly in hardware, and some microcontrollers have a fixed-depth stack that is not directly accessible"，与 claim 两个分句（部分小微处理器硬件实现栈、一些微控制器有不可直接访问的定深栈）逐一对应。
